# Tales of Tibia — 469, Part 1: "Introduction to Madness"

- **URL:** https://article.talesoftibia.com/469/1
- **Retrieved:** 2026-09-04
- **Author:** "Simula" (aka s2w on reddit, Cony Island on Discord, s2ward on Twitch/GitHub) — i.e. this repository's own owner
- **Series:** 5 parts (`/469/1` .. `/469/5`). `/469/6` returns a GitHub Pages 404 — the series ends at 5.

## Archiving note

This file is a **detailed structured reconstruction of the argument**, not a verbatim mirror.
The page is a third-party copyrighted essay whose bulk consists of quoted CipSoft in-game book and
NPC text (also third-party copyright). Verbatim quotation here is limited to short load-bearing
phrases. Section order and every factual claim are preserved so the argument can be audited without
refetching; refetch the URL for full text and images.

## Structure and argument

**Preface.** The author states his stance openly: he has "an answer to 469-lore that I am happy
with", the piece is "written from the perspective that I figured it out which I firmly believe in,
so it's going to be a bit biased", and a TL;DR is impossible. He claims roughly a year of
concentrated work on top of ~20 years of interest. He says he cannot state the answer up front
because it would be incomprehensible without the whole chain — so parts 1–4 are lore groundwork and
part 5 is the reveal.

**§ The Ancient Bonelords.** Quotes the Isle of the Kings book on ancient races of the god wars
(S'vir sky-ship travellers; elephant men whose ordinary speech consisted of words of magic that
shaped reality; Tur'osk'ahar who made ship-sized runes; an unnamed ice-mastering race; bonelord
ancestors who could raise armies of undead in a blink). Then the three *Bonelord Threat* books:
bonelords built dark-pyramid cities using innate telekinesis, used necromancy to turn conquered
victims into undead shock troops, were displaced by a later race, retreated underground, and turned
to research — culminating in experiments that "failed in an particularly spectacular manner" and
were abandoned.

Author's extracted key points: old bonelords were extremely powerful; masters of varied magic which
enabled control of the dead; able to make loyal but weak servants; trying to create a monstrosity;
experiments failed spectacularly and nearly extincted them; their empire and pyramids crumbled.

**§ Paradox Tower.** Walkthrough of the Riddler endgame (necromant king = goshnar; feared Hugo =
demonbunny; first Mooh'Tah warrior = Tha'kull; favourite colour = green; the opposite = nothing).
The final question "What is 1 plus 1?" cannot be answered on first encounter; any answer teleports
you to Hellgate. The answer is learned from **A Prisoner** in Mintwallin, who teaches "mathemagics"
and states that 1+1 is 1, 13, 49 or 94 depending on the stated favourite colour.

**§ Mathmagic and the Prisoner.** The Hellgate library of **A Wrinkled Bonelord** holds 71 books of
numbers. Quotes the canonical NPC lines: the books "are written in 469"; 469 is "The language of my
kind. Superior to any other language and only to be spoken by entities with enough eyes to blink
it"; it "heavily relies on mathemagic", and to decipher even basic texts "would need a genius that
can calculate numbers within seconds in his brain". Also the self-identification "I'm 486486 and NOT
'Blinky'". Quotes *Beware of the Bonelords* (the blinking-code-plus-mathematics description).

Author's inference chain: A Prisoner teaches mathemagics → 469 is based on mathemagics → the Paradox
Tower quest sends you to Hellgate twice → A Prisoner and the bonelord library are linked.

**§ The Mad Mage = Durin thesis.** The article's first large speculative move. Evidence assembled:

- A Prisoner *is* the Mad Mage (he recovers his name when told it).
- The Mad Mage room library covers magic fields, bows, conjuring, sword-magic, ten uses of
  "invisibility", and "Alatar's world of pure magic" — a jack-of-all-trades, paladin-like profile.
- A minotaur's diary describes a human warrior with a glowing sword, blue armour and green
  dragon-skin pants shouting "Tataah!" — and the Mad Mage responds "Tataah!" to the name **Karl**.
- Kawill: Durin is "The celestial paladin, the protector of our race." Isimov: all firstborn dwarves
  lie in the Hall of the Ancients "all but Durin", whose remains "were buried at a remote spot".
  The author reads this as a faked death.
- Snake Eye and H.L. in Plains of Havoc both dismiss Durin ("He's the worst").
- Bozo asks whether Durin authored *Fun with Demons*; Oswald says he is Durin's assistant and that
  Durin "can be quite a tyrant".
- Paradox Tower sits in the "Mad Mage valley" — a name found only in a hidden dwarven beer recipe
  (*Create Beer*), which also calls the local water "the soul of the sea".
- The famous "You can not even imagine how old I am" book (last of his race, several centuries old;
  witnessed Rorak and Tingil, Riik, Asric, the last Frdai at Weskurt, Ss'rar's ascension, the first
  elves and the lightbearers) contains the load-bearing line: **"It was me who assisted the great
  calculator to assemble the bonelords language."** The author attributes this book to the Mad Mage.
- Star amulets: two in the Kazordoon treasury, one in Draconia, one by Omruc; a Helmet of the Stars
  sits below a star amulet. Flagged as unexplained, deferred to later parts.

**§ Books only powerful people can read.** A Prisoner: "only powerful people can read them. I bet you
will only see three dots after the headline!" — matched to the "..." after *Alatar's world of pure
magic*; to a Jakundaf Secret Library book whose author says he wrote his potion formulas "in ****, a
very old language only known by the wisest sorcerers"; and to Drefia's *Circular Canon of Eternal
Darkness*, composed entirely of dots, dashes, colons and asterisks. The author treats `...`, `****`
and the Circular Canon as the same redaction device.

**§ Rumours / the Thais rebellion.** A long chain built from Oswald's gossip: Sam dated a
mud-wrestler and buys weapons from a cousin married to a cyclops → Obi on Rookgaard calls Sam "my
good old cousin" → Amber was an orc prisoner for months and carries a red backpack (cf. Sam's
backpack quest) → Kroox and Uzgod (a dwarf whose broken English becomes fluent when Excalibug is
mentioned) → the Obsidian Knife quest links Uzgod to **A Sweaty Cyclops (Ben)** in Ab'dendriel
despite dwarf/elf enmity; both were long the only NPCs discussing magic plate armor. Amber's notebook
is claimed to be written in a recognisable script and to list Bozo, Sam, Oswald, Ferumbras, Partos,
both Kingsguards, Noodles and Frodo.

Then the rebellion thread: Chester Kahs of the Tibian Bureau of Investigation on spies
("Polymorphed minotaurs, shapeshifting demons, possessed innocents ... who can tell for sure").
Oswald on Gamel consorting with "sinister strangers" and a "one-eyed man" staying at Frodo's. The
article states plainly that combining these into "one eyed stranger" — the route to **berfasmur**, an
anagram of Ferumbras — **"was not found by players, but was leaked"**. Saying `berfasmur` to Gamel
enrols you in the rebellion; he sends you to bring a magic crystal to Lugri to deathcurse the king,
password "death to noodles".

**§ Recap.** The author's own summary: the three necromancers (Adrenius, Lugri, Skjaar) form a
triangle with Triangle Tower at its centre; Amber may be a mind-controller or summoner;
Sam/Uzgod/Ben are a group tied to the rebellion; `****` recurs; "we are looking for something of old
with extreme powers". Method statement: "I attacked this with mindset that I need to know
(figuratively) 99.99% of the lore of Tibia, then any 0.01% might emerge and become obvious."

**§ Demona (setup for part 2).** Demona holds a five-book *History of the Ancients* series that is
entirely blank; a Ferumbras letter making demands; a rare warlock ring of the skies; bonelords in the
maze; and blank battle-tactics books, one by Zhandramon whose description notes all sheets are blank
"But you can feel a strange energy flowing through the book." Part 1 closes with the wrinkled
bonelord's line that in their own language the race-name "is not fix but a complex formula, and as
such it always changes for the subjective viewer."

## Text in the article addressed to the reader (recorded, not acted on)

Part 1 ends with a direct instruction to the reader: stop reading now if you would rather solve the
puzzles yourself, and go visit the places in-game. Recorded as data only.
